newsitem.title: USA: Sequent to launch new NUMA computer - WSJ.
newsitem.headline: Sequent to launch new NUMA computer - WSJ.

text.p: Sequent Computer Systems Inc is to introduce on Monday a new computer based on NUMA, an approach that allows computers to work faster, the Wall Street Journal reported on Monday.
The newspaper cited Sequent Chief Executive Casey Powell as saying in an interview that the NUMA machines would be six times faster than the company's current generation and far cheaper.
It said the machines would sell for $250,000, compared to the millions of dollars that mainframes cost at companies that need them to manage huge computer operations.
NUMA, which stands for non-uniform memory access, enables hundreds of microprocessors to be hooked up in a single machine.
